clinical_category: ARDS pathophysiology - alveolar-capillary barrier injury and permeability edema
blueprint_topic: Pathophysiologic response to acute diffuse lung injury and impaired gas exchange
stem: A nurse reviews the pathophysiology of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS). Which process best explains the development of impaired gas exchange in ARDS?

options.A: Inflammatory epithelial and endothelial injury increases alveolar-capillary permeability, causing alveolar edema and reduced gas exchange
options.B: Isolated elevation of left-ventricular filling pressure produces hydrostatic pulmonary edema without primary alveolar-capillary injury
options.C: Transient bronchial smooth-muscle constriction is the principal lesion and resolves the alveolar edema once bronchodilation occurs
options.D: Increased surfactant activity raises lung compliance and improves oxygen diffusion across the injured alveoli

rationale: A is correct. Current NCBI/StatPearls guidance describes ARDS as an acute diffuse inflammatory lung injury associated with capillary endothelial injury and diffuse alveolar damage. In the pathophysiologic process, epithelial and endothelial cellular injury causes inflammation and increased alveolar-capillary permeability, producing alveolar edema; the edema reduces gas exchange and contributes to hypoxemia and decreased lung compliance. B describes a hydrostatic cardiogenic mechanism rather than the permeability injury characteristic of ARDS. C reduces ARDS to reversible bronchospasm and does not explain diffuse alveolar damage. D is the opposite of the expected physiologic consequence because ARDS is associated with impaired gas exchange and decreased compliance.
educational_objective: Explain ARDS as diffuse inflammatory alveolar-capillary injury that increases permeability, produces alveolar edema, and impairs oxygen exchange and lung compliance.
source_version_date: StatPearls; last update 2024-01-31; current NCBI Bookshelf edition accessed 2026-08-18
source_locator: NCBI Bookshelf 'Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome' → Introduction: ARDS is an acute diffuse inflammatory lung injury associated with capillary endothelial injury and diffuse alveolar damage. Pathophysiology: pulmonary epithelial and endothelial injury is characterized by inflammation and increased alveolar-capillary permeability leading to alveolar edema; alveolar edema reduces gas exchange and causes hypoxemia; the injury manifests with impaired gas exchange and decreased lung compliance.
source_claim_supported: Current NCBI/StatPearls content directly supports inflammatory epithelial/endothelial injury, increased alveolar-capillary permeability, alveolar edema, impaired gas exchange, hypoxemia, and decreased compliance as the ARDS pathophysiologic sequence tested by the item.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation client-needs subcategory (11–17% of items), within Physiological Integrity; this item tests understanding of acute pathophysiologic alterations that threaten respiratory function.
correction_summary: Substantive rebuild. The source used a generic SCCM URL and bundled etiology, pathophysiology, severity, and treatment claims without an exact locator. The final item uses a current NCBI/StatPearls pathophysiology section and limits the construct to the directly supported alveolar-capillary permeability injury and gas-exchange consequences.
audit_findings: The original SCCM root URL did not provide an exact pathophysiology locator.
Current NCBI/StatPearls content directly supports epithelial/endothelial injury with increased alveolar-capillary permeability and alveolar edema.
The final rationale separates ARDS permeability edema from hydrostatic cardiogenic edema and does not assert an unsupported single etiology.
Distractors represent competing respiratory/pulmonary-edema mechanisms and none reproduces the ARDS alveolar-capillary injury sequence.
Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct answer, no second defensible mechanism, no unsupported numeric diagnostic criterion, no cueing, and no unresolved conflict.
